items.item: Replication slots persist across crashes and know nothing about the state of their consumer(s), which consumes storage because required WAL cannot be removed
max_slot_wal_keep_size specifies the maximum WAL a slot may retain before the server may remove WAL it still needed; the default of -1 retains without limit
restart_lsn is the oldest WAL still required by the consumer of a slot

sources.source: Debezium connector for PostgreSQL (WAL disk space consumption)

items.item: A low-traffic captured table inside a busier database, and a quiet database sharing WAL with a busy one, are both named cases where a healthy connector's slot does not advance

at.step: Reveal: confirming, not merely running, moves the marker

items.item: The hook's own premise — a connector reporting healthy for the entire duration a disk fills up — is confirmed as a necessary consequence of slot semantics, not an exaggerated scenario: a slot's own position is independent of connector liveness, measured directly.

The contrast between connector status and slot progress is demonstrated as a controlled comparison in a single function: the same total write volume split identically, with only the confirmation behaviour differing between the two slots measured.

The max_slot_wal_keep_size demonstration confirms the sandbox's own default (-1) before changing it, and resets it afterward and re-confirms the reset, so no other topic in this chapter inherits an altered cluster configuration.

The 'lost' status is not merely read from a column but proven consequential: a direct attempt to read from the invalidated slot afterward is shown to raise PostgreSQL's own real error, not a status flag with no enforced effect.

The idle-captured-table and multi-database variants are disclosed explicitly as sourced, not measured, because this sandbox has one database and no second instance to create the exact imbalance Debezium's own documentation describes.

The AWS RDS five-minute-invisibility case is named from Debezium's own documentation only, since no RDS instance is reachable from this sandbox, and is not conflated with the genuinely measured multi-database mechanism.

The wrong half of the first predict question — that healthy connector status implies a confirming consumer — is ruled out directly by the measured fact that a slot's own gap grows under a live, connected consumer that simply has nothing new to confirm.

items.item: The wrong half of the final predict question — that connector status is the right alert signal — is ruled out by the hook's own premise directly: the incident the topic opens with is exactly a case where that signal stayed green.

inactive_since, the PostgreSQL 17 column CHAPTER.md implicitly assumes for monitoring, is confirmed absent on this sandbox's PostgreSQL 16 server, so the lag-monitoring measurement uses only the columns actually available here (restart_lsn, confirmed_flush_lsn, active) rather than claiming one that doesn't exist.
This topic hosts the stalled-consumer leg of the 8.2 lab directly, per CHAPTER.md's own instruction, while re-snapshotting after a lost slot is explicitly left to topics 13-14, not attempted here.
